override.repo_standard: The implementer handoff explicitly required this class be 'modeled directly on the existing CommanderSpineBasisFields class in the same file -- read it first', and that sibling class already establishes the repo's convention of one self-contained class per gate/feature carrying its own pinned-HEAD fixture, expected-shape dict, and per-condition test methods.
override.reason: Size here is the established, sanctioned shape for this exact category of red-proof test (feature-scoped, self-contained, drift-guarded via skipTest-on-moved-HEAD) -- splitting it would scatter one cohesive gate's worth of fixtures/assertions across files for no locality gain, contradicting the pattern the handoff named as the model to follow.

smells.finding: The 5 artifact-kind promotion tests (plan.c1/c2/c4/c5, reconcile.c1) share one helper, _assert_artifact_discriminates, parameterized by wrong_type_evidence/adversary_payload/matching_payload -- exactly the DRY shape that avoids restating the 3-step wrong-type/wrong-match/matching drive per test.
EXPECTED_CHECKS/PRE_EXISTING_NONNULL are structured dicts/sets keyed by (task_id, cond_id) tuples, not stringly-typed primitives standing in for a real shape.
_assert_artifact_discriminates takes 4 params (cid, wrong_type_evidence, adversary_payload, matching_payload), each independently meaningful; no data clump to collapse.

init.c1's shell command does d.get('engine_session',{}).get('status') -- a 2-level defensive .get() chain matching the engine's own idiom at scripts/checklist_engine.py:1269/1285/1397/1433/1499, not an excessive chain.

All 8 promotions and the 3 collateral test fixes are concrete, driven by the handoff's named list and the actual broken pins; no speculative hook, unused parameter, or abstract-for-a-future-case machinery was added.

Inline rationale comments on each adversarial mutation (e.g. 'attacks the boundary the match does NOT cover') are explicit, one-line, and were a named handoff requirement ('log each mutation's own one-line rationale as a code comment') -- they document intent behind a genuinely non-obvious test-design choice, not compensate for confusing code.
